chapters.title: Assemble the portfolio from retained evidence
chapters.transcript:
You have reached the final lesson of Phase Two. Bring forward the work from all six journeys and the reviewed capstone from this week. A portfolio is an organized collection of evidence that shows what you did, how you made decisions, and what the result can support. It is not a collection of impressive claims. Its purpose is to let another person find and inspect the work behind your explanation.

Use PROGRESS Closeout: portfolio, review, ownership, gaps, roadmap, evidence, support, and sustain. Portfolio means assemble the required work. Review means inspect its accuracy, quality, and readiness. Ownership means explain your contribution and decisions. Gaps means record what is missing or unresolved. Roadmap means plan practical next actions. Evidence means identify what each action will show. Support means name the people, resources, and permissions needed. Sustain means decide how you will keep the work useful and responsible over time.

Start with the existing index and files. Locate a result from each of the six journeys. Retain the approved opportunity and strategy work, bounded workflow, people and adoption decisions, value and delivery work, operating and improvement evidence, and final demonstration and execution package. Use the requirements attached to your own completed lessons. Do not replace their actual evidence with a generic summary. Give each entry a meaningful name, current version, purpose, evidence reference, and status. A reviewer should be able to locate the item without guessing.

Add the functioning bounded artifact and its charter, test and revision evidence, final demonstration, responsible statement, positioning set, and continuation plan. These are the parts you have already developed. If one file supports several requirements, point to the relevant parts instead of making unnecessary copies. Keep the version history that explains a material correction. Do not make new versions of completed assignments merely to increase the size of the portfolio. Revise only when an actual gap, error, or review question requires a correction.

Our supplied fictional intake case has a retained tabletop artifact, complete-input test, missing-date test, absent-approval test, and a revision that makes the human delivery gate visible. The index can point to those records and the demonstration. It cannot claim live customer delivery, measured savings, or organizational permission that the example never established. Its labels must say fictional. Your own work may have a different permitted setting; describe that setting accurately.

Open your current index now. Check whether all six journey results and the final required components can be found. Mark an absent item as missing. Name the focused correction needed, rather than writing a polished sentence that hides the absence. This is how the portfolio becomes useful to both you and its reviewer.

chapters.title: Review ownership, gaps, and the final demonstration
chapters.transcript:
A complete-looking folder can still contain unsupported claims, private material, or unclear ownership. Review the actual final files and references. Check that sources are identifiable, the current version is clear, important tests can be found, and human decisions are explained. A link that opens the wrong draft does not establish the final result. A reference that another authorized reviewer cannot use needs an appropriate access or correction step.

Confirm that the evidence is safe to share with its intended reviewer. Remove private inputs where they are not needed. Label fictional, sanitized, or recreated examples accurately. Keep any necessary permission visible. Do not upload confidential records into AI simply because you want a quick completeness check. A privacy-safe index can identify the evidence and its status without exposing the underlying material.

Write a short growth reflection with a changed decision and an improved result. Explain what you first did or believed, what evidence led you to change, what you changed, and what the retained work now shows. In our fictional case, the earlier design treated complete information as permission to deliver. The revision kept human approval separate and made the hold state visible in the tabletop. That is a specific design change. It is not proof of live savings or a claim that all future errors have been prevented. Your reflection must cite your own observation and evidence.

Explain ownership honestly. Describe what AI drafted or suggested, what you inspected, and which choices you made. Do not erase AI assistance, and do not let AI assistance erase your judgment. Your ability to explain a decision in your own words is part of the evidence. An attractive output alone cannot show that you understand its purpose, limits, or review route.

Deliver the final demonstration of the bounded artifact. Show the ordinary path and a meaningful exception, then point to the test, revision, and human approval boundary. Use the current artifact, not a disconnected slide that implies functionality you cannot show. Retain the demonstration reference and actual questions. If no reviewer has yet asked a question, state that honestly; prepare plausible rehearsal questions but label them as rehearsal. Do not invent an academy response or permission.

Use the approved AI request to check the privacy-safe portfolio index for missing required evidence and unsupported claims. Inspect its suggestions against the actual records. AI may overlook a gap or invent a requirement. Record what you accepted, corrected, or rejected. It must not decide certification.

Identify any remaining issue and make a focused correction within the planned weekend window. Keep the before, after, and affected retest references where relevant. If evidence is still missing, record that status and the actual question for review. Your human review confirms that you inspected the package; it does not make a missing requirement complete or award a credential.

chapters.title: Plan thirty, sixty, and ninety days with evidence checkpoints
chapters.transcript:
Carry forward the primary opportunity, backup, and thirty-day evidence-building action from Lesson Six Point Five. Extend that action into a practical thirty-, sixty-, and ninety-day plan. A plan describes what you intend to do and what evidence will guide the next decision. It is not a record of completed results. For each stage, name the action, owner or collaborator, needed permission, boundary, evidence checkpoint, and the decision that follows.

At thirty days, choose a bounded step that fits your actual setting. In the supplied fictional case, the proposed author first seeks permission from the responsible person for a limited internal pilot. The pilot would use only agreed safe inputs, a visible human delivery gate, and retained observations. The thirty-day checkpoint asks whether permission was obtained and what the permitted trial actually showed. No real person has been assigned, and no pilot has occurred in this teaching example. The owner must identify the real person and agreement in an actual project.

If permission is unavailable, do not proceed with live customer inputs. Use the backup from Lesson Five: a permitted fictional review that keeps the unresolved organizational dependency visible. The checkpoint should record what happened and what remains unknown. A delayed permission is not a reason to invent approval or quietly expand the scope.

At sixty days, schedule a quality review based on the evidence retained from the first stage. Compare ordinary inputs, known exceptions, human review decisions, and corrections with the agreed requirement. Name who may review the work and how you will retain their actual questions. Check usability, privacy, and responsibility as well as whether the artifact runs. If a required condition fails, narrow or pause the next step and revise the affected part. Do not assume the earlier prototype proves reliability in a new setting.

At ninety days, make a decision about wider use, continued bounded practice, revision, or stopping. Define the evidence needed before expansion. The fictional case requires relevant tests, a usable review route, the responsible person's permission, and an explanation of any new input or audience. Wider use remains conditional. The plan should not declare success in advance or promise clients, income, employment, or certification.

For your own plan, make the actions feasible. An owner is the person accountable for carrying out the step. A collaborator is someone whose participation is needed; their availability must be confirmed rather than assumed. Record unknown costs, resources, access, and permissions as dependencies to check. Name the support you will seek and the backup if it is unavailable.

Read your three stages together. Does each stage use the evidence from the previous one? Is the next decision clear? Are the permissions obtained before the affected action? Save the plan in the existing capstone package. Your next ninety days should show responsible continued practice, with decisions that change when the evidence changes.

chapters.title: Submit the checked package and continue responsibly
chapters.transcript:
Bring the index and final files together for submission. The required package contains all six journey results, a functioning bounded artifact, test and revision evidence, the demonstration, and a defensible execution plan. Include the responsible statement and positioning set you prepared. Defensible means that you can explain the plan's actions, limits, dependencies, and evidence checkpoints using the work you actually retained.

Do a final file check. Confirm that the index points to the intended current versions, sources and version history are available, privacy-safe labels are correct, and your human decisions are clear. Check the final demonstration and the responses to actual questions. Record any focused correction and affected retest. Avoid creating new versions of sound completed assignments merely to make the final package look fresh.

Use the applied completion check from the master: completion requires all six journey results, a functioning bounded artifact, test and revision evidence, the demonstration, and a defensible execution plan. Resolve missing evidence through focused revision. If a component remains missing, say what it is. A checkbox or AI statement is not evidence that the component exists. The Academy's authorized reviewer uses the governing rubric for the credential decision. This lesson does not add a new rubric or let an AI tool award certification.

Submit the index, finished artifact, responsible statement, positioning set, and continuation plan by Sunday of Week Six using the established Academy submission route. Saving practice notes or workbook answers preserves your work; it does not send files to a reviewer or confirm that the Academy received them. Retain the actual submission reference or acknowledgment when available. If the destination is not yet confirmed, record that dependency and use the existing Academy support route to resolve it. Do not fabricate a receipt or review outcome.

Additional Academy review time is administrative. It is not an extra teaching week and does not create a Journey Seven. Use the planned weekend window for the remaining correction. Keep questions and any later reviewer decision separate from your own explanation of learning. You may be proud of your growth while still naming a limit or pending requirement.

Plan to sustain the work after the course. Keep useful evidence and current instructions where you can find them. Decide when to review quality, who owns corrections, what support you need, and when to pause use. A change in inputs, audience, or permission may require a new bounded check. The thirty-, sixty-, and ninety-day checkpoints help you decide whether to continue, revise, or stop based on evidence.

Finish your reflection in your own voice. Point to one changed decision and one improved result, then state the next action you own. Complete the connected workbook and save the closeout notes to your continuing Project Record. You have practiced using AI to assist your work while retaining human judgment. Continue with the verified result, the responsibilities you can explain, and the next decision your evidence can support.

demos.title: Build the thirty-, sixty-, and ninety-day plan
demos.transcript: This supplied continuation is a proposal, not completed activity. At thirty days, seek the responsible person’s permission for a bounded pilot using agreed safe inputs and retained observations. If permission is unavailable, use the permitted fictional-review backup. At sixty days, compare the retained evidence with the agreed requirement in a quality review. At ninety days, decide whether to continue, revise, stop, or consider wider use. Expansion requires relevant evidence and permission. Each stage names action, owner or collaborator, permission, boundary, evidence checkpoint, and next decision. No success, client, income, or certification is guaranteed.
